title: Engine Inlet Cowl — Acoustic Panel Impact and Erosion Repair

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Repair of impact damage and leading edge erosion on the engine inlet cowl acoustic panel, keeping the acoustic treatment effective where the scheme allows and recording where it does not.

sections.purpose: This repair restores impact damage or erosion on the inlet cowl acoustic panel, either with a flush plug that preserves the acoustic treatment or with a solid patch where it cannot be preserved.
sections.damage_assessment: Two things matter: whether the backing skin is holed, and how much acoustic area is lost. Tap test the damage boundary and mark it; the honeycomb crush usually extends beyond the visible dent. Where the backing skin is intact, the flush plug route preserves the treatment and the acoustic loss is limited to the plug area. Where the backing skin is holed, the solid patch route applies and the acoustic area under the patch is lost entirely. Keep a running total of lost acoustic area per cowl: the noise certification depends on it, and a cowl that has accumulated several small patches can be outside the certified condition without any single repair being outside its own limit.
sections.repair_procedure: 1. Remove the cowl in accordance with the applicable maintenance task and support it. 2. Tap test the damage and mark the boundary of the crushed core. 3. Measure the damage and check the backing skin condition with a borescope through an existing drain. 4. Where the backing skin is intact, machine out the damaged face skin and core to the plug diameter on the drawing. 5. Fit the replacement core plug and bond the flush face skin to the cure schedule. 6. Where the backing skin is holed, machine the damage to a rectangle and install the solid patch with the clip CIN956404-32 and the angle D5410113480805 as backing. 7. Install the fasteners wet with sealant and de-burr every hole first. 8. Where the leading edge erosion route applies, blend the eroded lip to the profile template and build up with the erosion-resistant scheme. 9. Restore the protective scheme. 10. Record the acoustic area lost and add it to the cowl running total. 11. Refit the cowl and check the flush condition at the joint with the fan case. 12. Do a leak check of the anti-ice ducting at the cowl.
sections.inspection_requirements: Tap test the whole repair and fifty millimetres beyond it at installation, and record the result. Repeat the tap test at every C-check for the life of the repair. Where the solid patch route was used, do an eddy current inspection of the perimeter fastener row every six thousand flight cycles. Report the cowl running total of lost acoustic area to Aeralis each time it changes; when it reaches the figure in the drawing note the cowl must be assessed against the noise certification and this repair scheme is no longer available for it.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Crushed core area up to 4 000 square millimetres with the backing skin intact for the flush plug route, or up to 8 000 square millimetres with the backing skin holed for the solid patch route. Not within 60 mm of the cowl joint.

repair_drawings.title: Flush core plug and solid patch details, inlet cowl acoustic panel

type_data.fastener_pattern: Solid patch route only: two rows, 22 mm pitch, 14 mm edge distance; the flush plug route uses no fasteners
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Neither route carries a fatigue life limit. Both carry a repeat tap test at every C-check, and the solid patch carries an eddy current inspection of the perimeter row every 6 000 flight cycles. The limit that actually bites is the cumulative acoustic area lost per cowl.
